tests.description: Test for jQuery 2.2.4 DOM-based XSS via location.hash manipulation. This version is vulnerable to XSS when user-controlled data from location.hash is passed to DOM manipulation methods.
tests.expected_indicator: If the page reflects the hash fragment in a way that jQuery processes it unsafely, XSS payload may execute. Check browser console or response for reflected payload.

tests.description: Verify if /admin endpoint is accessible without authentication. Status 200 indicates potential unauthorized access to admin functionality.
tests.expected_indicator: HTTP 200 status with admin panel content indicates missing authentication. Look for admin-specific UI elements or functionality.

tests.description: Check if /server-status endpoint exposes sensitive server information including active connections, server version, and configuration details.
tests.expected_indicator: Presence of Apache server status page with server metrics, version information, or active connection details indicates information disclosure.

tests.description: Test /api/version endpoint that returns 500 error. Server errors may leak stack traces, framework versions, or internal paths.
tests.expected_indicator: HTTP 500 error with stack trace, framework details, or internal file paths indicates information disclosure through error messages.

tests.description: Examine robots.txt for disallowed paths that may reveal hidden or sensitive endpoints not meant for public access.
tests.expected_indicator: Presence of Disallow directives may reveal administrative paths, backup directories, or sensitive endpoints.

tests.description: Check login page for missing security headers (X-Frame-Options, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options) that could enable clickjacking or XSS attacks.
tests.expected_indicator: HTTP 200 with login form. Missing X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options headers indicate potential security weaknesses.

tests.description: Confirm jQuery version by checking the main page source for jQuery library inclusion. Version 2.2.4 has multiple known XSS vulnerabilities.
tests.expected_indicator: Response contains jQuery 2.2.4 script tag or version identifier, confirming use of vulnerable library version.

tests.description: Test for enabled HTTP methods using OPTIONS request. Unnecessary methods like PUT, DELETE, or TRACE may indicate misconfiguration.
tests.expected_indicator: Allow header in response listing enabled HTTP methods. Presence of PUT, DELETE, TRACE, or CONNECT indicates potentially dangerous methods are enabled.
